-418-
The Scheme of Undergraduate International Program in 
Economics (UIPE) for International Students
1. Program Aim
Undergraduate International Program in Economics (UIPE) is an English-taught program with a duration of 4 years, 
aiming to nurture future leaders to make an impact on the world by empowering knowledge, charismatic leadership and 
global competitiveness in a diverse and dynamic global economy.
UIPE provides the student with a curriculum designed to gradually increase depth in a concentrated major, a 4-year 
Liberal Arts education, and rich overseas experiences. In fact, all students in this program are encouraged to study outside 
Chinese mainland for at least one semester. For students planning to go into industry and international organizations, interning 
overseas during the senior academic year is encouraged; for students planning to do PhD studies, more rigorous education in 
math and economic theory and recommendation to top PhD programs by directors will be oﬀered. 
2. Credits and Degree
For International students, UIPE requires the completion of no fewer than 124 credits, including no fewer than 26 credits 
of General Education Courses, 28 credits of Basic Courses in General Discipline, 38 credits of  Professional Core Courses 
(including 2 credits of Undergraduate Research or Industrial Practice, 6 credits of Thesis), and 32 credits of Professional 
Advancement Courses. Bachelor in Economics will be granted to those who meet the requirements of the degree by Fudan 
University.
3 Curriculum
3.1 General Education Courses (26 credits)
General Education Courses include General Education Core Courses and Specialized Education Courses.
3.1.1 General Education Core Courses
The students are required to earn 10 credits from the seven modules. As most module courses are taught in Chinese in 
the spring and fall semesters the students can take the module courses oﬀered by Fudan International Summer Session, Fudan 
International Winter Session, or transer some credits from an exchange stay.
3.1.2 Specialized Education Courses
The number of credits required is 16. See details in the study plan. 
3.2 Specialized Courses (66 credits)
Specialized Courses include Basic Courses in General Discipline and Professional Core Courses.
3.2.1 Basic Courses in General Discipline
The number of credits required is 28. See details in the study plan. 
3.2.2 Professional Core Courses
The number of credits required is 38.

①Advice on Undergraduate Research/Industrial Practice：
It is recommended that undergraduates in the program with an interest in further study choose to complete undergraduate 
research by serving as an RA for a faculty member to strengthen mathematics and economics theory education. Others with 
employment plans are advised to participate in industrial practice in multinational companies or international organizations 
around the world, with a focus on improving business-related skills.
② All the students are required to finish the thesis in English, and a Chinese abstract is also required.

minor program and other programs. Students are required to select one of the development paths under the guidance of the 
supervisor, and follow the guidance to take the courses.

3.3.2 Honor Program
Please refer to the implementation plan of the SOE's Honor Program for the curriculum setting and study requirements.
3.3.3 Cross-disciplinary Programs
Students must complete a minimum of 32 credits. In order to fulﬁll the course requirements, students must take course

-421-
package(s) oﬀered by department(s) other than SOE plus electives from all courses oﬀered by the university
See more details at https://jwc.fudan.edu.cn/zyxcssfa/list.htm and https://jwc.fudan.edu.cn/kxkxcssfawsxw/list.htm. 
Upon successful completion of a course package the student will receive a corresponding certiﬁcate.
3.3.4 Academic Minor Programs
Students must complete at least 15 credits from UIPE's professional advancement I and a minor other than the 
undergraduate majors under the economics category. For the curriculum of the minor programs  please refer to https://jwc.
fudan.edu.cn/fxxsxwxmssfa/list.htm. Upon successful completion of a minor program and satisfaction of Fudan University's 
degree and graduation requirements students will receive a corresponding minor certiﬁcate.      
3.3.5 Innovation and Entrepreneurship Programs
Students must complete a minimum of 32 credits. Students are required to complete one or two innovation and 
entrepreneurship ocourse packages. For the curriculum of the course packages please refer to https://jwc.fudan.edu.cn/
cxcyxcssfa/list.htm. 
Other Notes
(1) Students must choose their development paths at the end of the 4th semester. Assessment will be made 
by graduation regarding the completion of the courses for your path.
(2) Change of the path should be approved by the supervisor. Both minor programs and the professional 
advancement path can be credited towards a course package. Courses shared by the professional advancement 
path and another multi-development path are counted only once for credits.
